fields.title: Credit Terms sits under Payment Methods in Settings and opens on Active
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure all twelve standard terms are active and COD is the default for new customers.
  • Start on the Settings page.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. In the Settings menu, find the Finance group.
  2. Click "Credit Terms".
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Finance group shows "Credit Terms" directly below "Payment Methods".

Step 2:

  • The Credit Terms page opens.
  • Its header reads "Credit Terms", with a primary "New Credit Term" button at the top right and a "⋯" menu beside it.
  • Below the header are two tabs, "Active" and "Inactive", each followed by the number of terms in it, and the Active tab is selected.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11670 (Story 1, Credit Terms page and list), story SV-11680 (Story 11, Release day: what changes for existing users)

  • S1-R2: “The page header shows the title "Credit Terms" and, top right, a primary "New Credit Term" button (Story 3: Create or edit a credit term) with a "⋯" page menu beside it (Story 12: Credit Terms audit log).”
  • S1-R3: “Below the header are two tabs, "Active" and "Inactive", each followed by a count of the terms in it. The page opens on Active.”
  • S11-R4: “The Credit Terms page appears under Settings → Finance for every user with 'Settings → Finance'.”
  • Key Decisions, Permissions: “Viewing and using the Credit Terms page (the list, New Credit Term, Edit, Make Default, Deactivate, Reactivate, Delete) is governed by 'Settings → Finance', the same permission as Payment Methods.”

fields.title: The Active tab lists terms in the fixed order, Credit Hold last
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure all twelve standard terms are active and COD is the default for new customers.
  • Make sure the shop has five active terms of its own: term A due 10 days after the invoice date, term B due 30 days after the invoice date, term C due on day 1 of the following month, term D due on day 22 of the following month, and term E due on day 1 of the following month. Term E's name comes after term C's in A to Z order.
  • Other terms may also be listed; check only the order of the named rows.
  • Start on the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps: 1. Without clicking any column heading, read the Name column from top to bottom.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • COD is the first row, Due on Receipt the second and Credit Hold the last.
  • In between, the Net terms (standard and the shop's own) run by number of days, lowest first: Net 7, then term A (10 days), then Net 15, Net 20, Net 30, then term B (30 days, after Net 30 because ties sort A to Z by name), then Net 45, Net 50, Net 60, Net 90, Net 120.
  • After every Net term come the day-of-the-following-month terms by day: term C, then term E (both day 1, A to Z by name), then term D (day 22).

The order also has a place for "any other term A to Z" before Credit Hold; question 2 on Chris Ward's sheet (shared with him 23 Oct 2026) asks which terms those are. This case checks every kind a shop can create.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11670 (Story 1, Credit Terms page and list)

  • S1-R5: “Rows are listed in this order on both tabs: COD; Due on Receipt; every Net term (standard and the shop's own) by number of days, lowest first; every "day of the following month" term by day, lowest first; any other term A to Z; Credit Hold last. Ties sort A to Z by name. The same order is used in every customer and vendor Credit Terms dropdown.”
  • S1-R14: “The Active tab lists every active term; the Inactive tab lists every deactivated term, standard and the shop's own, in the same columns and order.”

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "1 List and row menus" ("Active tab: one table"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes.

fields.title: Design: New Credit Term window with Net days looks as designed
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Note today's date on the calendar of the location you work in (date A).
  • Work out date B: the date 14 days later.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Open the attached design picture ct-p3-01-new-credit-term-net-x-days.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
  • Start on the Credit Terms page, Active tab.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click "New Credit Term".
  2. Type "Net 14 Days" in Name.
  3. Type 14 in the Days box.
  4. Resize the browser window to 1536 px wide (for example, maximise it on a 1536 x 864 screen at 100% zoom).
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A window titled "New Credit Term" opens with a close × at the right.

Step 2:

  • Name reads "Net 14 Days".

Step 3:

  • The window matches ct-p3-01-new-credit-term-net-x-days.png: the Name box with its floating label and the grey hint "Up to 31 characters. Prints on invoices and goes to QuickBooks." under it.
  • Below, two rows with round option buttons: "Due Net X days" (chosen) with the Days box and "days after the invoice date" after it, and "Due day of the following month" with a greyed, empty Day box and pale "of the following month"
  • Under them a light-blue box with an info icon and blue text "Net 14 Days means payment is due 14 days after the invoice date. An invoice dated date A is due date B."
  • At the bottom right "Cancel" (white) and "Create Credit Term" (blue).
  • The Cancel style: this attribute depends on question 12 (drawn pictures or build pictures, not answered yet): for now compare it with the picture named here.

Step 4:

  • At 1536 px nothing overlaps, nothing is cut off and nothing needs a sideways scroll.
  • The layout described above is unchanged, only wider.

The two dates show as a short month and day.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11672 (Story 3, Create or edit a credit term)

  • S3-R1: “"New Credit Term" opens a window titled "New Credit Term"; Edit opens the same window titled "Edit Credit Term". The buttons are "Cancel" and "Create Credit Term" (New) or "Save Changes" (Edit).”
  • S3-R2: “The window holds:”
  • S3-R2, Name: “Name (required), focused on open, accepting at most 31 characters, with the hint "Up to 31 characters. Prints on invoices and goes to QuickBooks."”
  • S3-R2, the two options: “Two options, one chosen at a time: "Due Net X days" with a Days box followed by "days after the invoice date", and "Due day of the following month" with a Day box followed by "of the following month".”
  • S3-R3: “A new term opens on "Due Net X days" with both boxes empty and the Day box disabled. Only the chosen option's box is active; the other is disabled and empty.”
  • S3-R5: “While the chosen box holds a valid number, a blue information line below the options explains the term, using today's date as the example invoice date (S3-R16):”
  • S3-R5, Net line: “Net: "{Name} means payment is due {X} days after the invoice date. An invoice dated {today} is due {due}." For example: "Net 14 Days means payment is due 14 days after the invoice date. An invoice dated Oct 21 is due Nov 4."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Name field hint | "Up to 31 characters. Prints on invoices and goes to QuickBooks." | Hint under the field, always shown”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Valid Net term typed | "{Name} means payment is due {X} days after the invoice date. An invoice dated {today} is due {due}." | Blue information line, updates as the user types”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "3 New credit term and Inactive tab" ("New credit term: Net X days"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes, except where this held design case follows the design.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ct-p3-01-new-credit-term-net-x-days.png

The design's own words:

  • “New Credit Term opens this window. Two kinds only: "Due Net X days" (1 to 365) or "Due day of the following month" (1 to 31). No separate Due label above them. The Name field opens without any error.”
  • “Only the selected option's box is active (Days, with 14). The other option's box is greyed out (DS disabled field) and empty. Clicking a greyed box selects its option; switching clears the box you left.”
  • “Source: DS Modals (form body), DS Text field, DS Radio, DS Alert (info).”
